questions.q: Which side of the brain creates the sense of I?
a: The left side, which handles language and story
The right side, which handles movement
Both sides equally, through memory
The brain stem, which controls breathing
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the left brain is the storyteller that uses language to tell you who you are.

questions.q: Why does the summary call the self an illusion?
a: It is a story language tells about many parts
It is a memory planted in childhood
It exists only during deep sleep
It is created by other people's opinions
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the brain fools us into thinking we are something language can define, though we are many parts.

questions.q: How does the summary explain suffering?
a: We suffer when the brain recognizes an unpleasant pattern
We suffer because our needs are never met
We suffer when we ignore our emotions
We suffer because language is imprecise
questions.why: Lesson 2 says suffering arises when the brain matches what we see to a pattern it finds unpleasant.

questions.q: What activity helps activate the right brain?
a: Movement such as yoga or exercise
Reading and writing in detail
Solving math problems quickly
Making lists of goals
questions.why: Lesson 3 says movement-based activities like yoga, exercise or meditation engage the nonverbal right side.

questions.q: What comes with a more aware right brain, according to the summary?
a: Intuition and better decisions
Sharper language skills
Stronger memory for facts
Greater logical precision
questions.why: Lesson 3 says awareness of the right side brings intuition, and scientists find it helps decisions.
